ADR 0004 — The runtime owns the moments that must be right ​

  • Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-02 → 2026-10-11 (eighteen journey items in the first vertical), restated 2026-10-13

Context ​

With the whole journey model-led, measured over hundreds of chats: a required question was skipped 25–50% of the time depending on the run; a list published under the user's name was invented 1 in 64 chats even with a model-specific note; a model attested confirmed:true after the user sent a change; a correction was recorded without acknowledgement; a fetched record slid silently into the summary. Prompt rules moved these rates; none reached zero, and each model slipped somewhere else.

Decision ​

The model owns the conversation; the runtime owns the moments that must be right. A step is such a moment: the runtime draws it (a form, chips, a picker), reads the reply in code by its whole content, writes the draft, carries the values into every tool call, and tells the model one fact. A settle chains into the next owed step or the confirmation summary in the same reply; an owed step is late-drawn under a model turn with the model's own question cut; words beside an open ask go to the model and the ask is redrawn under the answer; a reload redraws the open ask; the review re-opens a step's own card and returns to the summary; dependencies re-ask what a change invalidates. Steps are data on the manifest (per type) and code in the domain (steps/index.ts) built from three helpers or the raw interface.

Rejected ​

  • "Stricter prompts": measured, insufficient, model-specific.
  • "Validate after the fact only": the wrong value had already been shown and confirmed.
  • "A form instead of a chat": loses the conversational gathering that the model does well.

Consequences ​

Runtime turns cost no tokens and are deterministic — evals pin them exactly; the model's prompt gets a short block of runtime facts per turn (cache-stable prefix, varying tail); every step reports a behaviour event (counts and enums only). The eval runner must answer runtime asks it did not script (it does: tap, submitForm).

Source: docs/adr/0004-runtime-owned-steps.md — edit it there; the site mirrors the repository.
